goblet_squat.name: Goblet Squat
goblet_squat.tierNote: Front-loaded squat pattern that self-limits load via grip and upper-back — excellent teaching and warm-up tool, but caps out well below a barbell squat as a growth stimulus.

box_squat.name: Box Squat
box_squat.tierNote: Breaking the eccentric at the box reduces stretch-shortening contribution, which is useful for concentric strength and rate of force development but removes the stretched-position stimulus that drives hypertrophy.

cossack_squat.name: Cossack Squat
cossack_squat.longLengthNote: deep lateral squat position loads the working hip at end range
cossack_squat.tierNote: Primarily a frontal-plane mobility and adductor-length movement. Loadable only lightly for most lifters, so it earns its place through mobility and adductor coverage rather than growth.

safety_bar_squat.name: Safety Bar Squat
safety_bar_squat.tierNote: Cambered bar shifts load forward and reduces shoulder external-rotation demand — a genuine option for lifters with shoulder or elbow restriction. Similar stimulus to a back squat, ranked slightly lower on hypertrophy only because the upright torso reduces hip contribution.

bulgarian_split_squat.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
bulgarian_split_squat.longLengthNote: rear leg hip flexors and front quad at length

walking_lunge.name: Walking Lunge
walking_lunge.longLengthNote: deep bottom position loads the trail-leg hip flexor and lead-leg glute at length
walking_lunge.tierNote: Unilateral loaded knee flexion through a deep range, same family as the Bulgarian split squat (S). Ranked one below it because the walking version caps practical load and demands more balance per unit of stimulus.

leg_extension.name: Leg Extension
leg_extension.tierNote: Per Kassiano et al. 2026 (PMID 41379528): leg extension produces significantly greater rectus femoris growth than back squat; back squat produces significantly greater distal vastus lateralis growth. Not interchangeable for regional quad development.

pistol_squat.name: Pistol Squat
pistol_squat.tierNote: A genuine strength and mobility feat, but balance and ankle dorsiflexion usually limit the set before the quads do — which caps its value as a growth stimulus. Kept mainly as a skill-goal target. Merged with a second entry filed as “Single-Leg Squat” — same movement, same tags, no implement between them. That entry rated it A/B/A with no stated reasoning; these tiers stand because they have some.

trap_bar_deadlift.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
trap_bar_deadlift.tierNote: More upright torso and load closer to the centre of mass than a straight-bar deadlift: lower spinal shear, higher peak power and velocity. Best power-tier hinge in the library; slightly less hamstring-specific than the RDL for hypertrophy.

rdl.name: Romanian Deadlift
rdl.longLengthNote: deep hip flexion loads hamstrings at length
rdl.stretchingRationale: Lengthened-position hamstring loading at the bottom of the hinge — per Alizadeh et al. 2022, full-ROM strength work matches dedicated stretching for ROM gains.

hip_thrust.name: Hip Thrust
hip_thrust.tierNote: Per Plotkin et al. 2023 (PMID 37461495): hip thrust and back squat produce statistically similar glute hypertrophy despite hip thrust showing much higher EMG amplitude — EMG did not predict the hypertrophy outcome. Squats additionally grew the quads/adductors; hip thrust did not. Filed under glutes rather than hips after merging with a duplicate entry (“Barbell Hip Thrust”) that was already filed there — the evidence above is entirely about glute hypertrophy, so glutes is where this belongs.

glute_bridge.name: Glute Bridge
glute_bridge.tierNote: Same hip-extension pattern as the hip thrust but with a far shorter loadable range and no easy way to add external load. Genuinely useful as activation/warm-up work; outclassed as a growth stimulus by the loaded Hip Thrust (S).

back_extension.name: Back Extension
back_extension.tierNote: Trains lumbar and hip extension through a long range against gravity. Modest loadability, but one of the few movements that directly targets the erectors in the lengthened position.

superman.name: Superman
superman.tierNote: Very low load and short range. Useful as an activation or rehab-entry drill; not a meaningful strength or growth stimulus for a trained lifter.

leg_curl.name: Leg Curl
leg_curl.tierNote: Maeo et al. (2021, MRI, 12wk within-subject) found seated leg curl produced greater hypertrophy than prone in the biarticular hamstrings. Generic/prone curl trains the shorter-length position, so it ranks below Seated Leg Curl (S) while still being the only movement that isolates biceps femoris short head. Merged with a duplicate “Lying Leg Curl” entry: lying is prone, so that was this exercise under another name. Its longLengthBias flag is not carried over — it hedged itself to “partially”, and this row’s own note is that the prone position is the SHORTER one.

nordic_curl.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
nordic_curl.tierNote: Regional hamstring hypertrophy from Nordic curls (knee-flexion emphasis) differs from hip-extension-dominant exercises like RDL — not fully interchangeable for complete hamstring development.
nordic_curl.stretchingRationale: Deep lengthened-position hamstring loading — Alizadeh et al. 2022 found full-ROM strength work produces ROM gains equal to dedicated stretching, with no added benefit from stacking extra static stretching on top.

incline_press.name: Incline Bench Press
incline_press.tierNote: Incline pressing shifts emphasis toward the clavicular (upper) pec region relative to flat pressing — not simply a flat-press substitute.

cable_fly.name: Cable Fly
cable_fly.longLengthNote: loaded stretch at the bottom position

lateral_raise.name: Lateral Raise
lateral_raise.tierNote: Cable and dumbbell lateral raises produce broadly similar lateral-delt hypertrophy despite different resistance-curve theory — equipment choice should follow comfort/progression/preference, not assumed superiority.

push_up.name: Push-up
push_up.tierNote: Kikuchi & Nakazato (2017) matched push-ups to 40% 1RM bench over 8 weeks and found no significant difference in pec or triceps thickness gains; Kotarsky (2018) replicated with progressive variations. Ranked A rather than S only because loading past bodyweight needs a vest or band.

dip.name: Dip
dip.longLengthNote: deep bottom position stretches the pec
dip.tierNote: Boettcher et al. (2010) found forward-lean dips produce pec activation comparable to bench press, and the movement loads near-bodyweight through a deep stretched bottom position. Easily weighted via belt, unlike most calisthenics.

preacher_curl.name: Preacher Curl
preacher_curl.longLengthNote: elbow extended against support at the bottom
preacher_curl.tierNote: Preacher and incline curls train the biceps at different joint angles/lengths and produce different proximal/distal hypertrophy patterns — not interchangeable for complete biceps development.

calf_raise.name: Calf Raise
calf_raise.tierNote: Straight-knee (standing) calf raises produce significantly greater gastrocnemius growth than bent-knee (seated) — well-supported (Kinoshita et al. 2023). The common belief that seated calf raises are specifically superior for soleus growth is weaker than often claimed: in the same study the standing-vs-seated soleus difference was not statistically significant, and ankle dorsiflexion range was not matched between conditions, limiting how much weight that specific comparison can bear.

tibialis_raise.name: Tibialis Raise
tibialis_raise.tierNote: Trains the tibialis anterior, which nothing else in a normal programme loads. Prescribed for ankle durability and shin resilience rather than size — its value is coverage, not tier.

atg_split_squat.name: ATG Split Squat
atg_split_squat.longLengthNote: deep knee and hip flexion under load
atg_split_squat.stretchingRationale: Full-depth lengthened quad/hip loading by design — per Alizadeh et al. 2022, this already provides the ROM stimulus dedicated static stretching would target.
atg_split_squat.tierNote: Same loaded unilateral deep-knee-flexion pattern as the Bulgarian split squat, with a deeper knee-over-toe position. Bloomquist et al. (2013) and Kubo et al. (2019) both found greater anterior-thigh, adductor and glute hypertrophy from deeper knee flexion, so the extra depth is a reason to rank it up, not down. Was previously mis-categorised as bulletproofing, which capped it below near-identical movements.

sissy_squat.name: Sissy Squat
sissy_squat.longLengthNote: rectus femoris loaded in a lengthened position
sissy_squat.stretchingRationale: Lengthened-position quad loading — per Alizadeh et al. 2022, full-ROM strength work matches dedicated stretching for ROM gains, so extra static stretching adds little here.
sissy_squat.tierNote: Isolates knee extension with the hip extended, putting the rectus femoris at a long length — an unusual and useful stimulus, but hard to load and demanding on the knee.

band_external_rotation.name: Band External Rotation
band_external_rotation.tierNote: Low-load rotator-cuff work. Prescribed for shoulder durability — the point is cuff endurance and scapular control, not hypertrophy, so tier understates its programme value.

wrist_curl.name: Wrist Curl
wrist_curl.tierNote: Direct wrist flexor work. Small muscle, small stimulus; included for forearm and grip durability coverage.

dead_hang.name: Dead Hang
dead_hang.tierNote: Isometric grip and shoulder decompression. Builds grip endurance and is well tolerated; no meaningful hypertrophy stimulus.

copenhagen_plank.name: Copenhagen Plank
copenhagen_plank.tierNote: Harøy et al. (2017, RCT) showed adding the Copenhagen adduction exercise to FIFA 11+ produced the eccentric hip-adduction strength gain the standard programme lacked; Ishøi et al. (2016) found large eccentric strength increases. Best-evidenced adductor movement in the library.

plank.name: Plank
plank.tierNote: Isometric anti-extension. Plateaus quickly for trained lifters — Ab Wheel Rollout (A) trains the same pattern through range under far greater demand.

hanging_leg_raise.name: Hanging Leg Raise
hanging_leg_raise.longLengthNote: abdominals loaded from a hanging, lengthened trunk position
hanging_leg_raise.tierNote: Loaded hip flexion plus anti-extension through a long range, with the abdominals stretched at the bottom. One of the better trainable core movements once a hang is comfortable.

seated_calf_raise.name: Seated Calf Raise
seated_calf_raise.tierNote: Per Kinoshita et al. 2023: soleus growth from seated (bent-knee) work was not significantly different from standing in this study, and ankle ROM was not matched between conditions — the gastroc/soleus split is directionally real (soleus does not cross the knee, so bent-knee doesn't disadvantage it the way it disadvantages the gastrocnemius) but the specific "seated is optimal for soleus" claim carries only moderate confidence.

reverse_fly.name: Reverse Fly
reverse_fly.tierNote: Merged with a duplicate “Rear Delt Fly” entry. Its dumbbell-or-machine equipment and its thoracic secondary are carried over — the mid-traps and rhomboids do work here — but its C/A/C tiers are not: both rows are coaching consensus, and this is the row that survives.

cable_lateral_raise.name: Cable Lateral Raise
cable_lateral_raise.tierNote: Cable and dumbbell lateral raises produce broadly similar lateral-delt hypertrophy — pick by equipment/comfort/preference, not assumed resistance-curve superiority.

overhead_tricep_extension.name: Overhead Cable Extension
overhead_tricep_extension.tierNote: The triceps long head crosses the shoulder joint — overhead positions train it at a longer muscle length. Comparisons of overhead vs. neutral-arm elbow extension have found greater triceps hypertrophy from the overhead position.

incline_db_curl.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
incline_db_curl.tierNote: Preacher/incline curls train the biceps at different lengths and produce different proximal/distal hypertrophy patterns than standing curls — not fully interchangeable.

seated_calf_raise_machine.name: Seated Calf Raise (machine)
seated_calf_raise_machine.tierNote: Bent-knee position biases soleus by shortening gastrocnemius. Pairs with a straight-knee variant rather than replacing it.

single_leg_calf_raise.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
single_leg_calf_raise.longLengthNote: deficit position allows full dorsiflexion stretch

seated_leg_curl.name: Seated Leg Curl
seated_leg_curl.longLengthNote: hip flexed — hamstrings held long throughout
seated_leg_curl.tierNote: Hip-flexed position trains the hamstrings at longer muscle lengths, which favours growth over the lying variant.

cable_pullover.name: Cable Pullover
cable_pullover.longLengthNote: lats loaded in full overhead reach

incline_dumbbell_press.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
incline_dumbbell_press.longLengthNote: increased shoulder extension at the bottom
incline_dumbbell_press.tierNote: Incline pressing biases the clavicular (upper) pec relative to flat pressing.

overhead_dumbbell_extension.name: Overhead Dumbbell Extension
overhead_dumbbell_extension.longLengthNote: shoulder flexed — triceps long head under stretch
overhead_dumbbell_extension.tierNote: Overhead positions load the long head at long muscle lengths, which outperforms pushdown-only work for total triceps growth.

hip_abduction.name: Hip Abduction
hip_abduction.tierNote: One row for the movement on all three implements, after merging “Cable Hip Abduction” and “Hip Abduction Machine” into it. Those rated it S and A for hypertrophy against this row’s B, all three on coaching consensus alone — an S on unsourced opinion is not a claim this app should be making about a hip abduction, so B stands.

farmers_carry.name: Farmer's Carry
farmers_carry.tierNote: Trains grip endurance under load alongside trunk bracing — the two limiters that most often cap rowing and deadlift volume.

dragon_flag.name: Dragon Flag
dragon_flag.longLengthNote: body held long, abdominals loaded at extended length
dragon_flag.tierNote: Anti-extension with the body at maximum lever length — the most demanding progression available without load. Scales by bending the knees.

weighted_decline_situp.name: Weighted Decline Sit-up
weighted_decline_situp.longLengthNote: decline allows the abdominals to stretch past neutral at the bottom
weighted_decline_situp.tierNote: Loaded spinal flexion through a range that extends past neutral, which is where the growth stimulus for rectus abdominis sits. Easily progressed by holding a plate.

suitcase_carry.name: Suitcase Carry
suitcase_carry.tierNote: Anti-lateral-flexion under real load, plus grip. The library had Pallof Press for anti-rotation but nothing loaded for frontal-plane resistance.

hollow_body_rock.name: Hollow Body Rock
hollow_body_rock.tierNote: Gymnastics-standard anti-extension position that transfers directly to the L-sit and front lever progressions already in the skill trees.

neck_harness_extension.name: Lying Neck Extension
neck_harness_extension.tierNote: Face down on a bench with your head past the end; a plate held on the back of the head once bodyweight is easy. Neck training is rarely reached by compound work. Progress load slowly and conservatively — this is a region where aggressive loading is not advisable.

neck_flexion.name: Lying Neck Flexion
neck_flexion.tierNote: Face up on a bench with your head past the end; a plate held on the forehead once bodyweight is easy. Progress load slowly and conservatively — this is a region where aggressive loading is not advisable.

sumo_goblet_squat.name: Sumo Goblet Squat
sumo_goblet_squat.longLengthNote: wide stance loads adductors through a longer range
sumo_goblet_squat.tierNote: Wide stance loads the adductors through a longer range than a conventional squat stance.

bodyweight_skullcrusher.name: Bodyweight Skullcrusher
bodyweight_skullcrusher.longLengthNote: elbows overhead — triceps long head loaded at length

sliding_leg_curl.name: Sliding Leg Curl
sliding_leg_curl.longLengthNote: hamstrings loaded as the legs extend away

levelDetails.advancementCriteria: Shift from passive stretch toward active straight-leg raises and seated pike compression — this is where active control of the new ROM starts getting trained, not just passive reach

levelDetails.holdOrRepTarget: 2-3x8-10 loaded pike or Jefferson curl progression
levelDetails.advancementCriteria: Add load here (Jefferson curl progression, loaded pike) — per Alizadeh et al. 2023, externally loaded work through range produces real ROM gains (bodyweight-only did not show the same effect in that meta-analysis), so this stage should genuinely involve resistance, not just deeper bodyweight folds

Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch comfortable on both sides before progressing to half split
Add active hip extension and active hamstring work alongside the static half-split hold — this stage is about control, not just deeper passive stretch
Split squat and long-length hamstring loading here — same rationale as pike stage 3: loaded work through range, not just assisted holds
Supported front split progressing to full front split, few cm off floor toward flat
Terminal goal — active front split under your own control; controlled oversplit only if genuinely appropriate for your goals, not a default target

levelDetails.holdOrRepTarget: 2-3x8-10 wide squat, or 2x20-30s Cossack each side
levelDetails.advancementCriteria: Wide squat and Cossack build active control of the wider stance — this is the access-to-control transition
Add load here (loaded Cossack, wide-stance strength work) — per Alizadeh et al. 2023, externally loaded work through range is the load-bearing stage, not just deeper bodyweight holds
Supported middle split, building toward less support over time
Terminal goal — full middle split with active end-range control, not just passive depth

Chest-to-floor pancake — the source document's own terminal example. Own extension for placement at level 5 specifically.

Ankle dorsiflexion is usually the limiting factor, so it's the explicit starting focus.
Own extension. Unassisted bodyweight hold, heels down, without support.
Own extension. Adding external load (goblet-held) — per Alizadeh et al. 2023, loaded work through range is a genuine mechanism for ROM improvement, not just deeper bodyweight holds.
Own extension. Full depth, heels down, no hands/counterbalance needed to hold the position.
Own extension — terminal integration stage: active deep squat with overhead reach or added load, using the ROM in a more complex position rather than just holding it.

Directly named in the source document (overhead squat). Light load, focus on maintaining the overhead position through the full squat.

MOBILITY_INTEGRATE_LIBRARY: Bear crawl to downward dog flow

hamstrings: single-leg RDL pattern, bodyweight x8 each side
shoulders: bear crawl shoulder taps, 10 each side
full_body: light general activation — easy cardio + dynamic stretch circuit
band circuit — pull-aparts, monster walks, good mornings
FIFA 11+ running series — forward, hip out, hip in, circling partner
adductors: Copenhagen plank, short lever 15s each side
lateral lunge to stand, 8 each side

adductors.foamRoll: Foam roll adductors, 60-90s each side, slow passes from groin to knee
adductors.pnf: Adductor PNF: press knees down against hands 6s → relax → deepen, 3-4 cycles
adductors.eccentric: Copenhagen plank, slow lower — 3 sets x 6-8 each side, short lever to start

hips.foamRoll: Foam roll glutes/hip flexors, 60-90s each side, pause on tender spots
hips.pnf: Banded hip flexor PNF: band-resisted hold 6s → relax → deepen stretch, 3-4 cycles each side
hips.eccentric: Deep split squat, slow 3s lower — 3 sets x 8 each side

hamstrings.static: Standing or seated hamstring stretch, 45-60s each side
hamstrings.pnf: Band-assisted PNF hamstring stretch: contract into band 6s → relax → pull deeper, 3-4 cycles each side
hamstrings.eccentric: Nordic hamstring curl eccentric — 3 sets x 5-6 (Henderson 2025: flexibility gains match static stretching)

quads_knees.dynamic: Walking lunges with a twist, 8-10 each side
quads_knees.pnf: Band-assisted quad PNF: contract 6s → relax → deepen, 3-4 cycles each side
quads_knees.eccentric: Reverse Nordic, slow lower — 3 sets x 6-8

calves.static: Wall calf stretch (both bent and straight knee), 45s each position, each side
calves.pnf: Band-assisted calf PNF against a step or band, 3-4 cycles each side
calves.eccentric: Deficit eccentric heel drop — 3 sets x 10-12 each side

ankles.foamRoll: Roll the underside of the foot with a ball, 60s each side
ankles.static: Kneeling ankle dorsiflexion stretch, 45s each side
ankles.dynamic: Ankle circles and alphabet tracing, both directions
ankles.pnf: Band-resisted dorsiflexion PNF: push into band 6s → relax → deepen, 3-4 cycles
ankles.eccentric: Loaded ankle rocker, slow — 3 sets x 10 each side

shoulders.static: Cross-body shoulder stretch + doorway pec stretch, 45s each
shoulders.pnf: Band-assisted shoulder PNF: contract into band 6s → relax → deepen range, 3-4 cycles each side

chest.foamRoll: Foam roll thoracic spine + chest opener over roller, 60-90s
chest.pnf: Band-assisted pec PNF: contract 6s → relax → deepen, 3-4 cycles
chest.eccentric: Deep push-up eccentric on handles, 3s lower — 3 sets x 6-8

biceps.foamRoll: Roll the front of the upper arm gently, 30-45s each side (light pressure — this area bruises easily)
biceps.static: Extended-arm wall bicep stretch, 30-45s each side
biceps.dynamic: Arm circles + light band curls, 10-12 reps
biceps.pnf: Band-assisted bicep PNF: contract into band 6s → relax → deepen, 3-4 cycles each side
biceps.eccentric: Slow-lower incline curl at full stretch — 3 sets x 8

triceps.foamRoll: Roll the back of the upper arm, 45-60s each side
triceps.pnf: Band-assisted tricep PNF: contract 6s → relax → deepen, 3-4 cycles each side
triceps.eccentric: Overhead extension, slow lower at full stretch — 3 sets x 8-10

forearms.static: Prayer stretch and reverse prayer, 30-45s each
forearms.dynamic: Wrist circles and tabletop rocks, 10 each direction
forearms.pnf: Wrist extensor PNF: press into the floor 6s → relax → deepen the rock, 3-4 cycles
forearms.eccentric: Slow-tempo wrist curl and reverse curl — 3 sets x 8-10

thoracic.foamRoll: Foam roll thoracic spine extensions, 10-12 slow passes
thoracic.static: Thread the needle hold, 30-45s each side
thoracic.dynamic: Cat-cow and open book rotations, 8-10 each side
thoracic.pnf: Not typically PNF'd directly — pair foam rolling with active rotation holds instead
thoracic.eccentric: Loaded pullover, slow lower — 3 sets x 8-10

lower_back.foamRoll: Avoid direct lower-back rolling — foam roll glutes/hips instead to offload it
lower_back.pnf: Band-assisted hip flexor/hamstring PNF (addresses lower back indirectly), 3-4 cycles
lower_back.eccentric: Bodyweight Jefferson curl, slow segmental — 3 sets x 5

full_body.foamRoll: Full-body roll: calves, quads, hamstrings, upper back, 30-45s each
full_body.static: Brief static hold circuit through major muscle groups, 30s each
full_body.pnf: Pick 1-2 tightest areas from above for targeted PNF work rather than doing all areas
full_body.eccentric: Slow eccentric circuit — pick one loaded stretch per restricted area, 3s lowers

ENGINE_SCENARIOS.description: Heavy lower-body + interval run
Heavy lower-body + easy run should score meaningfully lower conflict than heavy lower-body + quality run, even though neither crosses into combinable territory
Mild pain — should flag the exercise, not remove it
Significant pain — should skip the movement entirely
spineLoad:low exercise survives a HIGH back flag, clearly labelled
spineLoad:low does NOT bypass a HIGH shoulder flag on the same movement
Plateau despite good recovery — should suggest stimulus change, not fatigue
Performance decline should be detected
Rapid improvement should be detected
User consistently under-completes training
User consistently exceeds prescribed training
Missed workout should recalculate remaining demand, not cram
New user with no baseline should get a calibration message, not a fabricated number
5K goal and marathon goal at identical fitness should NOT get the same training architecture
Strength + running goal should split sessions by real priority weighting
A genuinely tight timeline should bias session focus toward strength, when load allows
Declining goal + rising load should trigger a strong deload signal
Checking the deload week box should actually reduce displayed sets on Today's plan, not just save a flag nothing reads
A strong signal (4+ corroborating) reduce recommendation should adjust weight, not sets or reps
A recently logged mobility session covering a domain should deprioritize it in future generation, even when it is the weakest assessed domain
Every domain-to-area mapping and every stretch-library key should be a real BODY_AREAS key, so charging and crediting agree on which body part a stretch belongs to
Every mobility domain should have five checklist rungs, a body area, a skill mapping and access/control/load exercises
